newsitem.title: USA: Abundant rain forecast for north Texas, Oklahoma.
newsitem.headline: Abundant rain forecast for north Texas, Oklahoma.

text.p: Several inches of rain and possibly flash flooding were forecast for much of Oklahoma and northern Texas Thursday to Saturday, meteorologists said.

The abundant rain could harm maturing wheat in those areas. However, only a small amount of rain was forecast for the dry fields in northern Kansas and Nebraska, not enough to aid the wheat there, they said.
Rainfall amounts of two to four inches were likely over the three days in northern Texas and in Oklahoma, and 0.5 to 1.5 inches across southern Kansas.
"It wouldn't be all that favorable," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist, referring to the effect of the abundant rain on Texas and Oklahoma wheat.
"There is a flash flood watch for the panhandle region (of Texas) and western Oklahoma," said Marshall Wickman, meteorologist with Wilkens Weather Techonologies.
WSC's Burgio said rain amounts should be less further north and wheat fields in northern Kansas and Nebraska may receive 0.1 to 0.3 inch.
Wickman said the storm system should slowly move northeast into the Ohio Valley and next week should produce 1.0 to 2.0 inches of rain in eastern Ohio.
